name: @kitora/collections
description: Kitora's collection components: one headless collection model (items, sections, selection, disabled, typeahead, virtual window, async loading, trees) with APG-correct Listbox, Select, Combobox, MultiSelect, TagsInput, Menu, Menubar, ContextMenu, Toolbar, TreeView (drag to reorder, inline rename, and a FileTree preset of folders and files), TreeSelect and Cascader on it.

exports.name: section
exports.description: Builds a section node.
exports.signature: <T>(id: string, label: string, items: readonly T[]) => Section<T>

exports.name: isSection
exports.description: True when `node` is a section.
exports.signature: <T>(node: CollectionNode<T>) => node is Section<T>

exports.name: isBranch
exports.description: True when an item can be opened: it has children, loaded or not.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(item: T) => boolean

exports.name: flatten
exports.description:
The visible rows in document order: section headers, then items, with the
children of expanded branches right after their parent. This is what a
listbox, menu or tree draws, and what a virtual window slices.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], options?: FlattenOptions) => CollectionRow<T>[]

exports.name: itemRows
exports.description: Only the item rows (the roving order).
exports.signature: <T>(rows: readonly CollectionRow<T>[]) => ItemRow<T>[]

exports.name: allItems
exports.description: Every item in the collection, depth first, sections opened.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[]) => T[]

exports.name: findItem
exports.description: The item with `id`, anywhere in the collection, or null.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], id: string) => T | null

exports.name: pathTo
exports.description: The chain of items from a root down to `id` (inclusive); empty when `id` is not there.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], id: string) => T[]

exports.name: groupRows
exports.description:
Groups flat rows into blocks for `role="group"` wrappers: each header starts
a block holding the items under it. With `grouped: false` (a virtual window,
where rows stay flat) the items after a header become loose blocks instead.
exports.signature: <T>(rows: readonly CollectionRow<T>[], grouped?: boolean) => RowBlock<T>[]

exports.name: CollectionItem
exports.description: The fields the kit reads from an item; a host's item type extends this with its own.

exports.name: SECTION_KIND
exports.description: Marks a node as a section rather than an item.

exports.name: Section
exports.description: A labelled group of items (APG `group` in a listbox, a labelled group in a menu).

exports.name: CollectionNode
exports.description: What a collection is built from: items, sections, or a mix of both.

exports.name: CollectionRow
exports.description: One rendered row: a section heading or an item at some depth.

exports.name: ItemRow
exports.description: An item row.

exports.name: FlattenOptions
exports.description: Options for `flatten`.

exports.name: RowBlock
exports.description: A run of item rows under one section heading (`section` null for loose items).

exports.name: normalize
exports.description: Lower case with accents stripped, so "Zürich" matches "zur".
exports.signature: (text: string) => string

exports.name: tokens
exports.description: The query split into normalized tokens; empty means "match everything".
exports.signature: (query: string) => string[]

exports.name: defaultMatch
exports.description: Every token appears in the label or in one of the keywords.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(item: T, query: string) => boolean

exports.name: filterNodes
exports.description:
Keeps the items that match and the ancestors of those that do; drops empty
sections. An empty query returns the input unchanged.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], query: string, match?: ItemMatcher<T>) => FilterResult<T>

exports.name: highlight
exports.description: Splits `label` into matched and unmatched parts for every query token (accent-insensitive).
exports.deprecated:
Use `queryRanges(label, query)` from `@kitora/ui/highlight` and render the ranges
with ui `Highlight` (or cut them with `splitRanges`), so every kit marks matches one way. One
difference: an empty `label` gives no parts there instead of one empty unmatched part.
exports.signature: (label: string, query: string) => HighlightPart[]

exports.name: ItemMatcher
exports.description: Decides whether an item matches a query.

exports.name: FilterResult
exports.description: What `filterNodes` returns: the kept tree, the branches to open, and the match count.

exports.name: HighlightPart
exports.description: A piece of a label, marked when it is part of the match.

exports.name: toggleSelection
exports.description: Clicking or pressing Space/Enter on `id`. Single mode replaces (or clears when `allowEmpty` and it was selected).
exports.signature: (selected: readonly string[], id: string, mode: SelectionMode, allowEmpty?: boolean) => string[]

exports.name: selectRange
exports.description:
Shift+click / Shift+arrow: selects every enabled id between `anchor` and
`target` in `order` (both inclusive) on top of what is selected. Without an
anchor in `order` it selects `target` alone.
exports.signature: (selected: readonly string[], order: readonly string[], anchor: string | null, target: string, isDisabled?: (id: string) => boolean) => string[]

exports.name: toggleAll
exports.description: Ctrl/Cmd+A: every enabled id, or none when all of them are already selected.
exports.signature: (selected: readonly string[], order: readonly string[], isDisabled?: (id: string) => boolean) => string[]

exports.name: SELECTION_MODES
exports.description: How a view selects: not at all, one item, or many.

exports.name: SelectionMode
exports.description: How a view selects: `none`, `single` or `multiple`.

exports.name: leafIds
exports.description: The enabled leaves under `item` (the item itself when it has no loaded children).
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(item: T) => string[]

exports.name: checkState
exports.description: Derived from the checked leaves: all checked, none, or some.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(item: T, checked: ReadonlySet<string>) => CheckState

exports.name: toggleChecked
exports.description: Toggling a checkbox: a fully checked item clears its leaves, anything else checks them all.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(item: T, checked: ReadonlySet<string>) => Set<string>

exports.name: cascadeColumns
exports.description:
The columns a cascader shows for an open path: the roots, then the children
of each item on the path that has them.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(roots: readonly T[], path: readonly string[]) => T[][]

exports.name: withChildren
exports.description: A copy of the tree with `children` set on the item `id` (async loading lands here).
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], id: string, children: readonly T[]) => T[]

exports.name: withLoaded
exports.description:
`items` with every loaded branch's children grafted on. The one place a
tree and its lazy loads become a single tree, so a picker's labels, paths
and check states read exactly the nodes its tree view shows.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], loaded: LoadedChildren<T>) => readonly T[]

exports.name: inheritCheck
exports.description:
The checked leaf ids after a lazy branch's children arrive. Before the load
the branch counted as its own leaf, so checking it stored the branch id;
once it has children that id names nothing (`leafIds` no longer returns it)
and would sit in the value as a stale pick while the branch reads
unchecked. So a checked branch hands its check down: its id leaves the value
and every enabled leaf under the new children joins it, after which the
branch derives "checked" from them like any loaded branch. An unchecked
branch, or a load that came back empty (the branch stays a leaf), returns
`checked` itself so a caller can skip the update by identity.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(checked: readonly string[], branchId: string, children: readonly T[]) => readonly string[]

exports.name: CHECK_STATES
exports.description: A tree checkbox's state (`aria-checked` true / false / mixed).

exports.name: CheckState
exports.description: A tree checkbox's state: `checked`, `unchecked` or `mixed`.

exports.name: LoadedChildren
exports.description: Children fetched by `loadChildren`, keyed by the branch id they belong to (in load order, so a nested branch follows its parent).

exports.name: treeFromPaths
exports.description:
A tree of folders and files from a list of paths. Shared prefixes become one folder; a path
ending in the separator is an (empty) folder; a repeated path appears once. Ids are the paths.
Siblings stay in the order they first appear; sort them with `sortFileNodes`.
exports.signature: (entries: readonly PathEntry[], separator?: string) => PathNode[]

exports.name: compareFileNodes
exports.description: Compares two nodes folders first, then by name in natural order.
exports.typeParameters: <T extends { readonly kind: FileNodeKind; readonly label: string }>
exports.signature: <T extends { readonly kind: FileNodeKind; readonly label: string; }>(a: T, b: T) => number

exports.name: sortFileNodes
exports.description: The tree with every level sorted: folders first then natural order (the default), as given (`none`), or by a comparator.
exports.signature: <T extends FileTreeItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], sort?: FileTreeSort<T>) => T[]

exports.name: extensionOf
exports.description: A file name's extension without the dot ("pdf" for "report.pdf", "gz" for "a.tar.gz"); "" for none or a dot file (".gitignore").
exports.signature: (name: string) => string

exports.name: stemOf
exports.description: A file name without its extension ("report" for "report.pdf", ".gitignore" for ".gitignore").
exports.signature: (name: string) => string

exports.name: pathOf
exports.description: The node `id`'s path from the root, its ancestors' labels and its own joined by the separator; null when it is not in the tree.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], id: string, separator?: string) => string | null

exports.name: renamePath
exports.description: A path with its last segment replaced by `name` ("src/a.ts" renamed to "b.ts" is "src/b.ts").
exports.signature: (path: string, name: string, separator?: string) => string

exports.name: movePath
exports.description: A path moved under the folder at `parentPath` (null or "" for the root): the parent path plus the last segment.
exports.signature: (path: string, parentPath: string | null, separator?: string) => string

exports.name: withPaths
exports.description: The tree with every node's `path` re-derived from the labels (after a move or a rename); ids are kept, and a node whose path and children did not change is the same object.
exports.signature: <T extends FileTreeItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], separator?: string, parentPath?: string) => T[]

exports.name: renameFileNode
exports.description: The tree with node `id` renamed to `name`, its path and every path under it updated; ids are kept.
exports.signature: <T extends FileTreeItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], id: string, name: string, separator?: string) => T[]

exports.name: childrenOf
exports.description: The children of the folder `parentId` (the root items for null); undefined when there is no such node.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], parentId: string | null) => readonly T[] | undefined

exports.name: siblingNameTaken
exports.description: Whether another child of `parentId` (the root for null) already has the name `name`.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], parentId: string | null, name: string, { exceptId, caseSensitive }?: SiblingNameOptions) => boolean

exports.name: parentIdOf
exports.description: The id of the folder holding node `id` (null at the root); undefined when the node is not in the tree.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[], id: string, parent?: string | null) => string | null | undefined

exports.name: FILE_NODE_KINDS
exports.description: What a file tree node is: a folder (may hold children) or a file.

exports.name: FileNodeKind
exports.description: What a file tree node is: `folder` or `file`.

exports.name: FileNodeFields
exports.description: The fields a file tree reads on top of the collection item (`id`, `label`, `children`, …).

exports.name: FileTreeItem
exports.description: A file tree node in the core: a collection item with the file fields.

exports.name: PathNode
exports.description: The plain node `treeFromPaths` builds.

exports.name: PathEntry
exports.description: One entry of `treeFromPaths`: a path, or a path with the file's details.

exports.name: DEFAULT_PATH_SEPARATOR
exports.description: The default path separator.

exports.name: FileTreeSort
exports.description: How a file tree orders siblings: folders first then natural order, as given, or a comparator.

exports.name: SiblingNameOptions
exports.description: Options for `siblingNameTaken`.

exports.name: toTreeNodes
exports.description: The items as dnd tree nodes: each item becomes `data`, its `children` (none = []) become nodes.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(items: readonly T[]) => ItemTreeNode<T>[]

exports.name: fromTreeNodes
exports.description:
The dnd tree nodes back as items: each node's `data` with `children` set to its nodes (an item
that had no `children` and still has none keeps it undefined, so a leaf stays a leaf). An item
whose children did not change is the same object.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly ItemTreeNode<T>[]) => T[]

exports.name: ItemTreeNode
exports.description: A node in the dnd kit's tree shape: the item as `data`, its children as nodes.

exports.name: fixedLayout
exports.description: A layout where every row is `rowHeight` px.
exports.signature: (count: number, rowHeight: number) => VirtualLayout

exports.name: measuredLayout
exports.description:
A layout of variable-height rows: `measured` heights where known, else
`estimate(index)`. Built as one prefix-sum array (O(count), fine for 100k
rows) and searched in O(log count).
exports.signature: (count: number, estimate: (index: number) => number, measured?: ReadonlyMap<number, number>) => VirtualLayout

exports.name: maxScrollTop
exports.description: The largest useful scrollTop: the content's end aligned with the viewport's end.
exports.signature: (total: number, viewport: number) => number

exports.name: rangeOf
exports.description:
The mounted slice of `layout` for a scroll position. A scrollTop past the
end (a list that just shrank) is clamped, so the last rows stay mounted
instead of an empty window.
exports.signature: (layout: VirtualLayout, scrollTop: number, viewport: number, overscan?: number) => VirtualRange

exports.name: virtualRange
exports.description: The mounted slice for a scroll position, fixed row heights.
exports.signature: ({ count, rowHeight, scrollTop, viewport, overscan }: VirtualInput) => VirtualRange

exports.name: scrollOffsetFor
exports.description:
The scrollTop that shows row `index` (clamped to the rows) with `align`,
clamped to the scrollable range. `auto` returns the current scrollTop when
the row is already fully visible. With no rows it is 0.
exports.signature: (layout: VirtualLayout, index: number, align: ScrollAlign, scrollTop: number, viewport: number) => number

exports.name: scrollToReveal
exports.description: The scrollTop that brings row `index` fully into view, or null when it already is (fixed heights; the roving source's scroll-follow).
exports.signature: (index: number, rowHeight: number, scrollTop: number, viewport: number) => number | null

exports.name: anchorShift
exports.description:
How far to move `scrollTop` so the rows on screen stay put when rows change height: the sum of the
changes of rows that START above the viewport's top (`layout` is the layout BEFORE the changes).
A row starting at or below the top only pushes content below it, so it needs no correction; at the
very top (`scrollTop` 0) nothing is anchored, and growth below is the reader's to see.
exports.signature: (layout: VirtualLayout, scrollTop: number, changes: readonly SizeChange[]) => number

exports.name: VirtualLayout
exports.description: Where rows sit along the scroll axis. Offsets are in px from the top of the content.

exports.name: VirtualInput
exports.description: Input to `virtualRange`: the row count, row height, scroll position and viewport.

exports.name: VirtualRange
exports.description: The mounted slice of a virtual list and the spacer heights around it.

exports.name: DEFAULT_OVERSCAN
exports.description: Rows above and below the viewport mounted ahead of scrolling.

exports.name: SCROLL_ALIGNS
exports.description: Where `scrollToIndex` puts the row: its top at the viewport's top, centred, its bottom at the viewport's bottom, or the least scroll that shows it (`auto`).

exports.name: ScrollAlign
exports.description: Where `scrollToIndex` puts the row: `start`, `center`, `end` or `auto`.

exports.name: SizeChange
exports.description: A row whose height changed: from its previous size in the layout to its newly measured one.

exports.name: splitTags
exports.description: Splits text on the delimiters: every complete piece, and the unfinished tail left in the input.
exports.signature: (text: string, delimiters?: readonly string[]) => { readonly pieces: string[]; readonly rest: string; }

exports.name: addTags
exports.description: Adds `candidates` to `tags` under the rules; returns the new list and what was rejected.
exports.signature: (tags: readonly string[], candidates: readonly string[], rules?: TagRules) => { readonly tags: string[]; readonly rejected: string[]; }

exports.name: DEFAULT_TAG_DELIMITERS
exports.description: Characters that commit a tag while typing or in pasted text (default comma, newline and tab).

exports.name: TagRules
exports.description: Rules for turning typed or pasted text into tags.

exports.name: POPUP_PLACEMENTS
exports.description: Where the popup goes relative to its anchor.

exports.name: placePopup
exports.description: The default positioner: flips above when there is no room below, clamps to the viewport edges, and opens submenus to the right (or left when that does not fit).
exports.signature: (request: PlacementRequest) => PlacedPopup

exports.name: AnchorRect
exports.description: The anchor's box in viewport pixels (the fields of a `DOMRect` the maths reads).

exports.name: PlacedPopup
exports.description: The answer of a positioner: the popup's fixed top-left and the height it may grow to.

exports.name: PlacementRequest
exports.description: What a positioner is asked: the anchor, the popup's natural size, the viewport and the wanted placement.

exports.name: PopupPlacement
exports.description: One of `POPUP_PLACEMENTS`: where the small placer puts a popup relative to its anchor.

exports.name: PopupPoint
exports.description: A point anchor (a context menu at the pointer).

exports.name: PopupPositioner
exports.description: The placement seam: our default is `placePopup`; any function of this shape replaces it.

exports.name: closesOnActivate
exports.description:
Whether activating an item closes its menu (and every menu above it). An action closes; a checkbox or a radio
stays open so several can be set in one visit. `closeOnClick` overrides the default for any kind.
exports.signature: (kind: MenuItemKind, closeOnClick?: boolean) => boolean

exports.name: MENU_ITEM_KINDS
exports.description: What an item does when activated: run an action, toggle a checkbox, pick a radio.

exports.name: MENU_SUBMENU_DELAY_MS
exports.description: How long the pointer rests on a submenu trigger before the submenu opens (Base UI's `delay`).

exports.name: menuItemRole
exports.description: The ARIA role for an item kind: `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`.
exports.signature: (kind: MenuItemKind) => MenuItemRole

exports.name: menuKeyCommand
exports.description:
The command for `event` in a menu, or null when the menu leaves the key alone (Tab, Escape and typed characters
are the layer's and the typeahead's). The inline keys follow the text direction: in RTL ← opens a submenu.
PageUp / PageDown do not move in a menu (Base UI's list navigation has no page jump).
exports.signature: (event: NavKey, context: MenuKeyContext) => MenuKeyCommand | null

exports.name: menuTriggerKey
exports.description: The arrow key on a menu trigger that opens the menu, and which end it lands on (APG Menu Button).
exports.signature: (event: NavKey, orientation?: RovingOrientation) => "ArrowDown" | "ArrowUp" | null

exports.name: MenuFocusOnOpen
exports.description: Where focus goes when a menu opens: an item at either end, the popup itself, or nowhere (it stays put).

exports.name: MenuItemKind
exports.description: One of `MENU_ITEM_KINDS`: an action item, a checkbox item or a radio item.

exports.name: MenuKeyCommand
exports.description: What a key does inside an open menu. `move` goes through the roving maths; the rest are menu rules.

exports.name: createRowIdFactory
exports.description:
A counter-backed id factory. The counter lives in the returned closure, not
in the module, so two editors (or a server and a client render) never share
a sequence.
exports.signature: (prefix?: string) => RowIdFactory

exports.name: isEmptyValue
exports.description: The default emptiness rule: an empty string, null or undefined.
exports.signature: (value: unknown) => boolean

exports.name: toRows
exports.description: Gives every pair a fresh id.
exports.signature: <V>(pairs: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[], nextId: RowIdFactory) => KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: reconcileRows
exports.description:
Re-ids `pairs` against the rows already on screen: the row at the same index
keeps its id, so an external reset that only edits text does not remount
every input (and lose focus). New indexes get fresh ids.
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], pairs: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[], nextId: RowIdFactory) => KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: isEmptyRow
exports.description: True when the row has a blank key and an empty value.
exports.signature: <V>(row: KeyValuePair<V>, isEmpty?: EmptyValuePredicate<V>) => boolean

exports.name: toPairs
exports.description: The pairs the app sees: ids dropped and (by default) empty rows trimmed.
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[], rules?: KeyValueRules<V>) => KeyValuePair<V>[]

exports.name: pairsEqual
exports.description: Pair-list equality by key and value (`Object.is` on values).
exports.signature: <V>(a: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[], b: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[]) => boolean

exports.name: addRow
exports.description: Inserts `row` at `index` (default the end; clamped).
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], row: KeyValueRow<V>, index?: number) => KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: insertRows
exports.description: Inserts several rows at `index` (default the end; clamped).
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], added: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], index?: number) => KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: removeRow
exports.description: Removes the row with `id`; unknown ids leave the list as it was (same reference).
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], id: string) => readonly KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: updateRow
exports.description: Patches the key and/or value of the row with `id`; the id never changes.
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], id: string, patch: Partial<KeyValuePair<V>>) => readonly KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: moveRow
exports.description: Moves the row at `from` to `to` (both clamped); out-of-range `from` is a no-op.
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], from: number, to: number) => readonly KeyValueRow<V>[]

exports.name: duplicateKeyIds
exports.description:
Ids of every row whose (non-blank, trimmed) key appears more than once. All
occurrences are flagged, not only the later ones, so the user sees both
sides of the clash.
exports.signature: <V>(rows: readonly KeyValueRow<V>[], rules?: Pick<KeyValueRules<V>, "caseSensitive">) => ReadonlySet<string>

exports.name: parseEnv
exports.description:
Parses `.env` text into pairs, in order. Blank lines and `#` comments are
skipped, `export ` is dropped, the key is everything before the first `=`
(trimmed). Values: `"double"` (escapes `\n \t \r \" \\`, may span lines),
`'single'` (literal) or bare (trimmed, a ` #` starts a comment). Lines with
no `=` or a blank key are ignored. Repeated keys are all kept, so the editor
can show the clash instead of silently dropping one.
exports.signature: (text: string) => KeyValuePair[]

exports.name: serializeEnvLine
exports.description: One `.env` line for a pair; values that need it are double-quoted with escapes.
exports.signature: (pair: KeyValuePair) => string

exports.name: serializeEnv
exports.description: `.env` text for the pairs, one line each, in order; `parseEnv` reads it back to the same pairs.
exports.signature: (pairs: readonly KeyValuePair[]) => string

exports.name: looksLikeEnv
exports.description:
True when pasted text should split into rows instead of landing in one key
input: it has a line break, or it is a single `KEY=value` line.
exports.signature: (text: string) => boolean

exports.name: pairsFromObject
exports.description: Pairs from an object, in its key order.
exports.signature: <V>(object: Readonly<Record<string, V>>) => KeyValuePair<V>[]

exports.name: pairsToObject
exports.description:
An object from pairs; blank keys are skipped and, for repeated keys, the
last one wins. `Object.fromEntries` defines own properties, so a key such as
`__proto__` is stored as data rather than replacing the prototype.
exports.signature: <V>(pairs: readonly KeyValuePair<V>[]) => Record<string, V>

exports.name: KeyValuePair
exports.description: One pair as the app stores it. `V` is the value type (a string by default; a select's id, a secret ref…).

exports.name: KeyValueRow
exports.description: One editor row: a pair plus a stable id that never changes while the row lives (React key, drag id, focus target).

exports.name: RowIdFactory
exports.description: Makes a fresh row id each call.

exports.name: EmptyValuePredicate
exports.description: Says whether a value counts as empty for trimming; the default treats `""`, `null` and `undefined` as empty.

exports.name: KeyValueRules
exports.description: Options shared by the row helpers.

exports.name: freeTextValue
exports.description: The value typed `text` stores; see the file header. Disabled items still match: the text names them, picking is not involved.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], text: string) => FreeTextValue<T>

exports.name: freeTextLabel
exports.description: The text a free-text combobox shows for a stored value: the label of the item with that id, else the value itself.
exports.signature: <T extends CollectionItem<T>>(nodes: readonly CollectionNode<T>[], value: string | null, known?: T | null) => string

exports.name: FreeTextValue
exports.description: What a free-text combobox stores for some typed text: an item's id with the item, the text itself, or nothing.

exports.name: rankItems
exports.description: The items matching `query`, best match first; an empty query keeps every item in order.
exports.signature: <T extends Rankable>(items: readonly T[], query: string, limit?: number) => T[]

exports.name: Rankable
exports.description: What the ranker reads from an item.

exports.name: mentionAt
exports.description:
The mention the caret is in, or null. A trigger counts only at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening bracket (so an email
address's `@` does not open the list), and the query runs from it to the caret with no whitespace in between. Of several triggers, the one
nearest the caret wins.
exports.signature: (text: string, caret: number, triggers: readonly string[]) => MentionMatch | null

exports.name: replaceMention
exports.description: Replaces the mention `match` covers with `insert` plus a trailing space, and returns the new text and where the caret goes (after the space).
exports.signature: (text: string, match: MentionMatch, insert: string) => { readonly text: string; readonly caret: number; }

exports.name: rankMentionItems
exports.description: The items to offer for `query`, best match first, through the shared ranking (label as the title, keywords as keywords).
exports.typeParameters: <T extends { readonly label: string; readonly keywords?: readonly string[] }>
exports.signature: <T extends { readonly label: string; readonly keywords?: readonly string[]; }>(items: readonly T[], query: string, limit: number) => T[]

exports.name: MentionMatch

The children `loadChildren` has fetched, by branch id. Leave it out and the
tree keeps them itself (lost when it unmounts); pass it with
`onLoadedChange` when a host must keep them across remounts or read the
loaded nodes too (TreeSelect does both: its popup tree remounts on every
open, and its chips label loaded children).

props.description: The host's rule for a drop (only folders take children, a locked branch takes nothing, …); default every drop the tree rules allow.

exports.name: inheritCheck
exports.description:
The checked leaf ids after a lazy branch's children arrive. Before the load
the branch counted as its own leaf, so checking it stored the branch id;
once it has children that id names nothing (`leafIds` no longer returns it)
and would sit in the value as a stale pick while the branch reads
unchecked. So a checked branch hands its check down: its id leaves the value
and every enabled leaf under the new children joins it, after which the
branch derives "checked" from them like any loaded branch. An unchecked
branch, or a load that came back empty (the branch stays a leaf), returns
`checked` itself so a caller can skip the update by identity.

props.description: Whether to show an × that clears the value.

props.description: What the closed field shows for the selected item (default its icon and label).

props.description: What the popup says when there are no options (default "No options").

props.description: Class names for the closed field.

props.description: Controlled selected id (null for none); leave undefined to let the select keep its own, seeded by `defaultValue`.

props.description: The id selected at the start when uncontrolled.

props.description: Controlled open state; leave undefined to let the picker keep its own, seeded by `defaultOpen`.

props.description: Whether the popup starts open when uncontrolled.

props.description: Called when the popup opens or closes, with the new state.

props.description: Accessible name of the field when there is no visible label.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called when focus enters the field (the popup takes focus while it is open, so this fires on arriving and again on coming back).

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called when focus leaves the field (a form marks the field touched here).

props.name: onChange
props.type: (id: string | null, item: T | null) => void
props.description: Called when the selection changes, with the id and the item (both null when cleared).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the field is disabled.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: a hidden input submits the chosen id under it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while nothing is selected; default a localised "Select…".

props.name: invalid
props.description: Whether to draw the field as invalid (`aria-invalid`).

props.name: items
props.description: The options and sections to choose from.

props.name: popupHeight
props.description: Max height of the popup in px.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description: Whether to lay the popup over the field so the chosen option sits on the value it replaces (off: the popup opens under the field).

props.name: virtualized
props.description:
Mount only the options in view (a long list): `true`, or `{ rowHeight }` (every row is `rowHeight` px, default 28). The keys, typeahead and focus
still reach every option. The popup then opens under the field (`alignItemWithTrigger` is ignored).

props.name: onBlur

props.description: Whether to lay the popup over the field so the chosen option sits on the value it replaces (off: the popup opens under the field).

props.name: virtualized
props.description:

props.description:
Form field name: a hidden input posts the value (the picked item's id, or the typed text with
`freeText`; empty while nothing is picked) under it, so the combobox submits with a native form.
The visible input has no name, so the label text is never posted. Disabled posts nothing.

props.description: Async options for a query (replaces `items`).

props.description: How a static option matches the query; default the label and keywords.

props.description:
Whether the typed text is itself a value: `onChange(text, null)` on every keystroke, or the item's id
when the text equals its label exactly; a `value` that is no item id shows as text.

props.description: One more option after the matches (and "Create …"), always shown while the popup is open.

props.description: Single-key overrides of the `collections-combobox` catalog (an `I18nProvider` translates the rest).

props.description: Accessible name of the chevron button per state (default the catalog's `hideOptions` / `showOptions`); wins over the catalog.

exports.name: ComboboxPopup
exports.description:
The anchored popup holding the `role="listbox"`. Focus stays in the input (arrows and Enter there drive the list), and a press on the popup keeps it there. The listbox is
named like the input: the same labelledby ids (they win over aria-label, as on the input), else its aria-label, else the text of a `<label htmlFor={id}>` (axe
`aria-input-field-name` wants every open listbox named).

Holds the loading, error and "no matches" rows. While the list has no items it is the primitives' `Combobox.Empty`: it tells the root that the popup shows something

exports.name: pressFocusesInput
exports.description:
The `onMouseDown` of a field box (`fieldClass`, `role="group"`): a press on the box itself or on
its static parts (chips' text, icons, padding) focuses the input, and `onPress` runs (a picker
opens its popup). `preventDefault` keeps the press from first blurring an input that already has
focus, so the popup does not close and reopen. Presses on the input or a button inside are left
alone. Keyboard users reach the input with Tab, which is all the box adds for a pointer.
exports.signature: (input: HTMLInputElement | null, onPress?: () => void) => (event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void

exports.name: ROW_HEIGHT
exports.description: Row and control height in px (h-7); the virtual window counts in it.

exports.name: surfaceClass
exports.description:
A popup surface (listbox, menu, tree popup; also the inline Listbox). It reads the design-language `menu` slot's radius,
fill and blur as `var(--dk-menu-…, <Kitora value>)`; the kit keeps its own `shadow-lg` and 5px rows. Rows highlight with the
slot's colours, and their parts follow (see `rowClass`).

exports.name: rowClass
exports.description:
One option / menu item row. It highlights on `:focus` (roving) and `data-highlighted` (the Select and Combobox options add
the fill); while highlighted or open it sets `--row-muted` and `--row-mark`, the colours its parts read through `mutedClass`
and `markClass` (kitora: the parts' own colours; a language with a brand-colour highlight: its foreground).

exports.name: groupLabelClass
exports.description: A section heading inside a list or menu.

exports.name: fieldClass
exports.description: The closed control of a select, combobox, tree select or cascader.

exports.name: chipClass
exports.description: A removable chip in a multi-select or tags input; its corner is the design-language `chip` slot's (`var(--dk-chip-radius, <its own>)`).

exports.name: markClass
exports.description: A check mark: primary, or what a highlighted row asks for (`--row-mark`). A caller's `text-*` replaces it.

exports.name: mutedClass
exports.description: Secondary text: muted, or what a highlighted row asks for (`--row-muted`). A caller's `text-*` replaces it.

exports.name: cn
exports.description: Joins class names (strings, arrays, `{ class: condition }` objects) and lets a later Tailwind class win over a clashing earlier one.
exports.signature: (...inputs: ClassValue[]) => string
